stem:
Meena adds two spoons of sugar to a glass of water and stirs. After some time, no sugar grains can be seen, yet the whole glass of water tastes sweet.

Which statement best explains this?

options.text: The sugar particles spread out and occupy the spaces between the water particles, so sugar is present throughout the water.
The sugar particles melt into a liquid and float on top of the water, making it sweet.
The sugar disappears completely, and only its sweetness stays behind in the water.
Each water particle absorbs a sugar particle inside itself, which makes the water particle sweet.

teacher.key_rationale: On dissolving, sugar particles separate and occupy the spaces between water particles, so sugar is present uniformly throughout the solution even though no grains are visible. B wrongly treats dissolving as melting; C claims the sugar vanishes; D incorrectly places sugar particles inside water particles rather than in the spaces between them.
